newsitem.title: BRAZIL: GM to announce new Brazil factory - paper.
newsitem.headline: GM to announce new Brazil factory - paper.

text.p: General Motors Corp. is expected to announce plans to build a third car factory in Brazil, the newspaper Jornal do Brasil reported.

The factory would involve an investment of around $600 million to produce a compact car similar to the Ka recently announced by Ford Motor Co., the newspaper said on Saturday. It said an announcement could come as early as next week, the report said.
The facility will probably be located in Minas Gerais or Santa Catarina and the company has already contacted various Brazilian banks and the government concerning the operation.
GM's decision to build the factory reflects demand for compact cars, which account for six of every 10 cars sold in Brazil, the newspaper said.
The company's Corsa has already proven a success in Brazil but GM has preferred to increase production of this line in Argentina.
If confirmed, GM would join a long list of international car manufacturers including Volkswagen, Toyota, Honda, Ford, Renault and Audi that have announced new investments in Brazil in recent years.
GM officials in Detroit were not immediately available to comment.
